messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate on serve-east-1a-pool-3 — RDMA retransmit surge + multiple serving containers restarted (node flaps). Auto-fallback attempted but some sessions saw 503s. Paging oncall.

maria: I'm on it, grabbing context. which customers affected?

incident-bot: Affected routes: /v1/generate (heavy), /v1/chat. Top impacted tenant ids: T-042, T-198 (sporadic errors). Latency spike ~2-3x, error rate 12% over 5m. Logs show repeated "ib_retry_exceeded" + kernel level "mlx5: QP timeout" messages.

raj.k: seeing kernel dmesg from node serve-3b: "mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: RQ overrun, flush qp" then containers restarted by kubelet. Also slices of CUDA errors right after: ``
[2026-03-15T14:13:27Z] runtime error: cuda runtime error (2) : out of memory at inference.cc:482
[2026-03-15T14:13:27Z] killing container redwood/serve:task-xyz (OOM)
``

sasha: oncall handoff: @maria you have pager. Raj, can you isolate which nodes flapped and if it's rack-local or multipath? I'll start mitigation steps in parallel.

raj.k: flaps on serve-3b, serve-3c, serve-4a — all share IB fabric bind 65:00.* same spine link. Multipath entries show increased retransmits across paths -> looks like a transient fabric hiccup causing higher latency which leads to kvcache thrash and then memory pressure across containers.

maria: mitigation plan: 1) cordon serve-3* nodes 2) drain non-critical pods 3) switch live traffic off to pool and start controlled failover to serve-east-1b-pool-1 4) enable model-fallback to gptx-8b-quant on the router for affected tenants 5) engage eng-sre for infra-level fix. Executing now.

kevin: +1 on fallback. Also suggest disabling cross-node KV cache to avoid thrash during fabric instability: set REDWOOD_KVCACHE_CROSSNODE=false on router for pool. That should reduce redispatch and memory blowouts.

maria: running commands:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon serve-3b
kubectl drain serve-3b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
# quick traffic shift
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/pools/route -d '{"from":"serve-east-1a-pool-3","to":"serve-east-1b-pool-1","weight":1.0}'
# set env to disable cross-node kvcache
kubectl set env deployment/router REDWOOD_KVCACHE_CROSSNODE=false -n redwood-serving
```

maria: drain completed for serve-3b, moving to 3c. Observed a few 503s during drain window but overall error rate trending down.

elana: I'm opening an incident status note for customer-facing comms. Draft: "We experienced elevated errors and latency in east cluster due to network fabric instability affecting some inference nodes. We've failed over traffic and applied mitigations; we're monitoring. No data exposure. ETA for stabilized service 30-60m." Anybody object to wording? :memo:

support-bot: Logged incident to INC-2026-0315-01 and linked to T-042 and T-198. Notifying customer success.

raj.k: quick snapshot of kernel errors on serve-4a (tail):
```
Mar 15 14:12:53 serve-4a kernel: mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: QP 0x1a2c0 state error, retry count exceeded
Mar 15 14:12:53 serve-4a kernel: mlx5_core 0000:65:00.0: reported timeout on qp 0x1a2c0
Mar 15 14:12:55 serve-4a systemd: kubelet: killing container redwood/serve-abc (oom)
```

sasha: eng-sre pinged and will loop in infra PM. Immediate ask: can infra flip to secondary spine route / move affected leaf off contested fabric? Raj / infra needed.

maria: observed another pattern — when the node receives sustained retransmits, the serving agent retries requests and rehydrates KV-cache which triggers spike in GPU memory usage -> OOM. So both network and serving retry policy contribute.

kevin: temporary tweak to serving config until fabric healthy: reduce max_concurrent_requests_per_gpu and lower batch size. Commands:
```
kubectl set env deployment/serve --namespace=redwood-serving MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS=6
kubectl set env deployment/serve --namespace=redwood-serving MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=256
```

maria: applied those env changes to pool router. Monitoring metrics in console: token throughput down but error rate normalized to ~1.5%.

elana: customer comms sent for impacted tenants: "we're seeing degraded performance; we've failed over and applied mitigations; we'll follow up with RCA." CS asked for ETA — told them 45m.

incident-bot: :information_source: Auto-snapshot saved to /incidents/3951236789/snap-20260315-1414.tar.gz (logs + perf metrics).

raj.k: infra update: we've diverted leaf switch sx-12 to backup path and applied IB firmware rate-limiting quirk on ports to reduce microburst. Watching fabric counters.

sasha: good. once fabric counters stabilize, plan is to uncordon nodes and gradually reintroduce kvcache cross-node. Action items: - infra to confirm fabric stable - eng-sre to verify driver/firmware errors - runtime team to prepare patch to backoff retries when IB retran rate > threshold - ops to run canary traffic to verify.

maria: handoff: I'll stay on for next 30m then hand to @sasha for follow-up runbook. If error rate climbs >3% re-page.

sasha: taking handoff at 15:45Z. Please post any outstanding logs. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

support-bot: Updated incident status: Mitigation in place, monitoring. Next update 15:45Z.
